order: Bucket review findings by provenance and close the running-process rule gap. A calibration audit found the cross-vendor reviewer accurate but miscalibrated: severity did double duty, so hardening shortfalls drew MAJOR beside genuine contract violations and REVISE became near-universal. Require every finding to carry a [BREACH] or [GAP] bucket alongside severity, and key the verdict rule on the bucket — a CRITICAL or MAJOR BREACH forces REVISE; GAPs of any severity, and MINOR BREACHes, permit APPROVE with the findings as dispatcher backlog. The same probe also refuted the protocol document's claim that every command-running role carries the never-end-a-turn-on-a-running-process rule: two top-level roles and the three architect launchers lack it. Give all five that rule, phrased for their failure shape. IN SCOPE: the reviewer brief's finding format and verdict rule; one added rule paragraph per role file; the changelog entry and the version stamp. Constraint: in the role files, add the new paragraph and leave every other line as it stands.
claims: Every finding now carries a [BREACH] or [GAP] bucket beside its severity, and the verdict rule keys on the bucket: a CRITICAL or MAJOR BREACH forces REVISE, while GAPs and MINOR BREACHes permit APPROVE with the findings listed as dispatcher backlog. The never-end-a-turn-on-a-running-process rule was added to all five command-running roles, phrased for each one's failure shape; no other line in those files was touched. Changelog entry and version stamp recorded. Verified: frontmatter lint 37 passed, 0 failed; the installer's lint checked 19 files with 0 errors and 0 warnings.
